Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a complex problem by calling itself to handle smaller, simpler versions of that same problem. Think of it like a set of Russian nesting dolls, where you must open each smaller doll one by one until you finally reach the solid piece in the very center. In programming, this stopping point is called the base case, which is a specific condition that tells the function when to stop calling itself so it does not loop forever. Once the base case is reached, the function stops and passes its answer back up through all the previous layers to successfully solve the original task.
